The person wakes very early (around 05:00) and leaves for work, returns in the late afternoon, but also has a late return (23:02) on some days, suggesting a shift pattern or overtime. The multiple rest periods (bed_pillow) indicate fragmented sleep, possibly due to shift work. Weekend days (Saturday and Sunday) show a later wake-up (no early badge/vest events) and a relaxed routine (phone on sofa, bath mat use, dining chair at table, coffee mug and plate put away), consistent with a day off. This reinforces the shift work hypothesis. The evening bath mat (18:35) and fork at sink (18:50) indicate a return home and dinner, consistent with a late afternoon/evening return. The coffee mug at sink at 20:52 suggests evening cleanup. No contradictory evidence. Day 8 (Tuesday) shows a later start: keys, phone, work_badge at elsewhere at 13:02, doormat at entry_hook_e1 at 11:56 (likely return) and again at 19:17 (evening return). This suggests a different shift or a day off with errands, but still consistent with a non-standard schedule. Day 9 (Wednesday) shows a thermos at counter at 05:00 (likely preparing a drink for work), a nap at 13:49 (midday rest), hi-vis vest at locker at 15:01 (return from work and storing gear), and evening dining chair and plate events (dinner at home). This pattern of early morning preparation, midday nap, and afternoon return with gear storage is consistent with a shift worker who may have a later start or a split shift. Day 10 (Thursday) shows a later start: hi-vis vest at elsewhere at 13:18, nap at 13:30, bath mat at 14:07 and 16:12, doormat at 15:59 and 21:46, keys at counter at 22:38. This pattern of a midday nap, afternoon return, and late evening return with keys suggests a split shift or a day with two outings, consistent with a non-standard schedule. Day 11 (Friday) shows a very early phone event (04:50 at entry_hook_e1, then 05:05 at elsewhere), a midday return (doormat at 12:38), afternoon bath mat (13:52, 13:55), dining chair at table (14:07), and an early evening nap (bed_pillow at 19:49). This pattern of early wake-up, midday return, afternoon hygiene and meal, and early evening rest is consistent with a shift worker who may have a morning shift and returns home by early afternoon, then rests. The absence of work gear events (hi-vis vest, badge) on this day could indicate a day off or a different shift type, but the early phone and midday return still suggest a non-standard schedule. Day 12 (Saturday) shows a relaxed weekend pattern: no early events, a dining chair at table at 14:16 (afternoon meal), and phone at nightstand at 21:01 (evening bedtime). This is consistent with a day off. The evidence consistently points to a non-standard schedule with varying start times, early morning preparation, midday naps, and use of work gear. The weekend pattern is distinct and relaxed. No evidence of a second resident.
